name: ProgressBar
purpose: Communicate determinate process completion from 0 to 100.
intent: Provide linear and circular visualizations driven by one read-only value model.

semantic.stopOnTrack: chart/sequence/brand/900 (contrasts with the light remaining track underneath)
semantic.stopOnProgress: chart/sequence/brand/300 (contrasts with the dark progress fill underneath)

componentForbidden: a fixed border/background pairing on the stop shape - it is a single flat fill that swaps token by segment

behaviorRules: Clamp rendered and announced value to 0–100.
Do not add animation unless explicitly specified.
Linear width is controlled by the parent.
Circular progress starts at 12 o'clock and advances clockwise.

Each track-stop mark renders in the color that contrasts with the segment currently underneath it, not one fixed color: the linear start stop uses the track-contrast color only at value = 0 and the progress-contrast color for any value > 0; the linear end stop and the circular top stop use the track-contrast color for value < 100 and the progress-contrast color only at value = 100.
compositionRules: May appear beside process labels or status summaries.
Do not expose Figma-only segment and stop parts as public components.
Do not compose with interactive thumbs or controls.
contentRules: Accessible labels identify the process, not only the percentage.
Visible percentage text is supplied by surrounding composition, not built into the component.
responsiveRules: Linear variant fills available inline width.
Circular diameter remains fixed at the current tokenized size.
themeRules: Do not use primitive color values in component CSS.
Both variants must work in light and dark themes.
do: Use linear for available horizontal space.
acceptanceCriteria: Linear and circular variants render from one numeric value API.
Both sizes match the documented anatomy.
Progress semantics and accessible naming are correct.
